# 1.26.2 — formulas no longer overlap the next line

A small fix for how formulas are drawn inside chat replies.

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## What was wrong

A formula placed inside a line of text (not on a line of its own) did not reserve room for the
part that hangs below the text baseline — the denominator of a fraction, a subscript, a tall
bracket. The next line was printed right over it. A worked example that put the condition
"(x ≠ −1)" on the line under a sum of fractions showed the condition on top of the denominators,
and a paragraph right after such a line touched them.

A formula inside **bold** or *italic* text, or in a heading, kept the fixed line spacing of plain
text and could run into the neighbouring lines the same way.

Two smaller defects in the formulas themselves:

- a minus sign with nothing on its left — "x ≠ −1", "(−2)", "−b" at the start — was spaced as
  subtraction and read as "x ≠ − 1";
- a slanted italic letter ran into what followed it: in "2(1 − a)" the "a" touched the closing
  bracket, and the exponent in "x²" sat on the letter.

## What changed

- A formula inside a line now tells the line where its baseline is, so the line makes room both
  above and below it. Nothing is drawn over a denominator any more.
- A formula anywhere in a paragraph or a heading — including inside bold, italic or a link —
  loosens that paragraph's line spacing.
- A minus (and other operation signs) with no left operand sits right next to its number.
- An italic letter gets a small extra space on its right, the same italic correction TeX applies;
  a subscript still sits close under it.

## File

`Amarin-Admin-AI-v1.26.2-win-x64.exe` — a single file, nothing to unpack.
